name: Spectrum TG480RTTR Rear-Tine Petrol Cultivator - 211cc, 48cm Working Width
Body Copy: Breaking new ground, clearing a neglected vegetable plot or turning stony soil asks more of a cultivator than a front-tine tiller can give. The Spectrum TG480RTTR is a rear-tine machine: it drives forward under its own power while the heavy-duty rotors cut independently, so you steer rather than wrestle. A 211cc 4-stroke OHV engine sends drive through a belt transmission that soaks up the shock when tines hit stones or roots. The rotors work a 48cm width down to 20cm deep, enough to prepare a proper seed bed or reclaim a tired lawn. A two-speed gearbox with reverse lets you back 72kg out of a tight corner, and pneumatic tyres keep the machine planted on uneven plots.
Unique Selling Point 01: Rear-tine design powers into hard, stony and uncultivated ground
Unique Selling Point 02: 211cc 4-stroke OHV engine runs cleaner and quieter than side-valve
Unique Selling Point 03: 48cm working width with up to 20cm digging depth
Unique Selling Point 04: Two-speed gearbox with reverse backs the 72kg machine out of corners
Unique Selling Point 05: Belt-drive transmission absorbs shock loads from stones and roots
Unique Selling Point 06: 3.6-litre fuel tank and 0.6-litre oil capacity for long sessions
Unique Selling Point 07: Pneumatic-tyred drive wheels stay steady on uneven plots and allotments
Selling Copy: A rear-tine cultivator built for the ground that defeats lighter tillers. The 211cc OHV engine and belt drive power heavy-duty rotors across a 48cm width and down to 20cm deep, while a reverse gear and pneumatic tyres make 72kg of machine easy to manoeuvre on stony or uncultivated plots.
